item.title: atlassian.com: 68. The gap: schema fields.
item.description:
Every page has a title, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But 162 structured data items miss a property Google expects.
The lesson for every team: Fill the required properties of each JSON-LD type, then test it in the Rich Results Test.
One automated analysis of public pages on 21 Oct 2026, requested through QA-lab URL Review. A starting point, not a verdict. The full report: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review.html?live=u-atlassian-com&utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=requested-reviews&utm_content=u-atlassian-com
#StructuredData #SEO #GEO #QA #QAlab

item.title: co.computrabajo.com: 68. The gap: HSTS.
item.description:
Every page has a title, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But HSTS is not sent.
The lesson for every team: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a max-age of at least a year, so browsers never try plain http again.
One automated analysis of public pages on 22 Oct 2026, requested through QA-lab URL Review. A starting point, not a verdict. The full report: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review.html?live=u-co-computrabajo-com&utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=requested-reviews&utm_content=u-co-computrabajo-com
#WebSecurity #HSTS #HTTPS #QA #QAlab

item.title: cgb.edu.co: 55. The gap: framing.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But other sites can frame the page.
The lesson for every team: Send frame-ancestors 'self' in the CSP, or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, so other sites cannot frame your pages.
One automated analysis of public pages on 25 Oct 2026, requested through QA-lab URL Review. A starting point, not a verdict. The full report: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review.html?live=u-cgb-edu-co&utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=requested-reviews&utm_content=u-cgb-edu-co

item.title: onepagelove.com: 81. The gap: form labels.

item.description:
HSTS tells browsers to never load your site over plain HTTP again. It takes one line of configuration on most hosts.
Try this today: Run curl -sI on your domain and look for strict-transport-security. If it is missing, add it at your host or CDN.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=tips-2026-10&utm_content=hsts

item.title: One h1 per page, saying what the page is.
item.description:
Logos and slogans often grab the h1. Search engines and screen readers both use it to understand the page.
Try this today: Read only the h1 of your top ten pages. Would a stranger know what each page is?
